secciones.texto: Darius Cooper is currently one of the most popular waiver wire additions, added in over 780,000 leagues within 24 hours. The second-year wideout for Philadelphia has accumulated 45.9 PPR fantasy points across six games in 2026, averaging 7.7 points per contest. His fantasy production spiked in Week 4 against Los Angeles with 18.3 PPR points on two receiving touchdowns, followed by 15.1 points and a touchdown against Jacksonville in Week 5. However, he cratered in Week 6 versus Carolina, posting just 1.9 PPR points on a single catch.

While fantasy managers are racing to claim Cooper, his game log reveals extreme volatility. He has relied heavily on touchdown efficiency rather than steady target volume, catching just three passes in Week 4 and two in Week 5. Additionally, he put up a zero in Week 3 against Chicago. Looking ahead to Week 8, Philadelphia visits Washington, a defense allowing the seventh-most PPR points to wide receivers at 35.9 per game. Despite this favorable matchup on paper, Cooper's low floor makes starting him a massive risk for fantasy rosters.

Our FX Model remains skeptical of Cooper's immediate fantasy impact, ranking him as the WR100 for Week 8. Projections sit at just 4.8 PPR points, 4.0 Half-PPR points, and 3.2 Standard points. These conservative metrics underline that while he serves as a solid depth stash for deep leagues, he cannot be trusted in starting lineups. His path to fantasy relevance requires a significant uptick in target share and opportunity. For now, treat him strictly as a bench hold while monitoring his weekly role with Philadelphia down the stretch.
